title: cairn help lists all, operator, cairn, then every device alphabetically
intention: `cairn help` prints its sections in the order [all], [operator], [cairn], then every other device with a bin under the instance root in alphabetical order, each listing the device's bin scripts with the first comment line of each; `cairn <device> help` lists that one device's bin; help is answered before the floor is laid, so it is called, returns, and is done.
why: Measured 2026-11-05: bin/cairn has no help branch (2026-11-05: `grep -n help bin/cairn` finds no case for it); an unknown device word is refused by name and a non-verb word falls to the self-named launcher (bin/cairn:207-213). Akien 2026-11-05 (Q#27, outline 8.4): 'if there's a script for it, run it, else get on the bus' and 'cairn help lists [all] then [operator] then [cairn] then the rest in alpha order'.
traces_to: Telos: the operator's one interface (outline 8.4). Law 1 (a shortcut is a settled route), Law 4 (script-else-bus is the dispatch, not a convention), RULE 1 (the bus is a device's public interface).
how: A `help` case in bin/cairn ahead of the floor. `cairn help` prints [all] (cairn.tools.base.shim.cold_list's root verbs with their meanings — help among them, child 2d6c1c36f3bd), then [operator], [cairn], then every other device under the instance root alphabetically, each section that device's bin shortcuts from cold_list. `cairn <device> help` asks the device's list over the bus (help answers as list) and, when the bus does not answer, prints cold_list for that device in-process with one line saying views need the bus. Child 2d6c1c36f3bd proves first.
falsifier: (1) over a scratch CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT holding devices zeta, operator, alpha and cairn, `cairn help` prints section headers in the order [all], [operator], [cairn], [alpha], [zeta]; (2) each section lists every executable in that device's bin with its first comment line, and a non-executable file is absent; (3) `cairn alpha help` prints only alpha's section; (4) help exits 0 with a scratch root whose postgres socket is absent (no floor is laid). (5) the [all] section lists help and every key of cairn.tools.base.shim.ROOT_VERB_SEMANTICS with its meaning, and a key added to that table in a fixture appears under [all] with no change to bin/cairn.

decisions.text: Red-first proof bin/proofs/test_cairn_help_lists_in_the_operators_order.py, check()/FAILURES/main() shape, one tooth per falsifier clause, PROVES = {'2e6c93cf74c7': {'1': 'clause_1', '2': 'clause_2', '3': 'clause_3', '4': 'clause_4', '5': 'clause_5'}} (tooth names written at build). Scratch roots only — no live bus, no live store.

Run the proof red, build, run it twice serially green plus the component's existing proofs. Commit before the hollow reading; seal with bin/cairn test --seal <path>.

decisions.source: Akien 2026-11-05: 'help can just call list'; answer open-ae78c6e4700d
decisions.text: [all] and every device section come from cairn.tools.base.shim.cold_list (the base tool's public interface), never hand-listed; bin/cairn holds no copy of the verb table or of the bin-reading rule. A future all-device verb (Akien's example: pid) appears by joining ROOT_VERB_SEMANTICS. Outline 8.4.3.1-8.4.3.2.
